# Lexicon index

GENERATED by tools/build_index.py on 2026-09-24. 350 entries, 2070 Hebrew headwords. Do not edit by hand.

**How to use this file.** It is a table of contents, not the guide. Find your Hebrew
word in the headword list, open the entry it points to, and apply that entry's
*Bottom line*. The entry is where the words are actually told apart, with each
distinction attributed to the authority who makes it, and disagreements between
authorities laid out rather than flattened. Part 2 below gives each entry's full
ruling so you can often decide without opening anything.

Each entry in Part 2 carries its *Bottom line* and then its *Rendering guidance*.
The Bottom line says what the words mean and how the authorities separate them;
the Rendering guidance is the one place in this guide that says how to put them
into English, and it is not on the website, only here.

---

Where a row names an English rendering, that rendering is that word's own.

its Bottom line; open it rather than guessing from the neighbouring words.

| דיברות | dibros | **sayings, Decalogue** | the Aseres HaDibros at Sinai, spoken to an assembled audience (Rabbi Klein); Hashem's absolute will, standing whether or not anyone follows it (Rav Hirsch); expectations that feel demanding (Rabbi Klein); better Ten Sayings than Ten Commandments | [speech-dibbur-amirah.md](entries/speech-dibbur-amirah.md) |

| חגור | chagor | **belt** | the general term, anything that goes around the body, whether at the torso, the heart, the waist or the feet (Malbim); the feminine chagorah carries the same sense | [hat-and-belt-mitznefes-migbaas-avnet.md](entries/hat-and-belt-mitznefes-migbaas-avnet.md) |
| חגורה | | see entry | one of the *hat and belt* words | [hat-and-belt-mitznefes-migbaas-avnet.md](entries/hat-and-belt-mitznefes-migbaas-avnet.md) |
| חד | chad | **one** | echad with the aleph clipped for brevity (Radak), once in Hebrew and otherwise Aramaic; lacking the aleph of oneness, it is the language Adam was demoted to (Rabbi Yehonosson Eybeschutz) | [one-echad-achad-chad.md](entries/one-echad-achad-chad.md) |
| חדה | | see entry | one of the *one* words | [one-echad-achad-chad.md](entries/one-echad-achad-chad.md) |

| חדל |  | **** |  | [earth-taivel-arka-cheled.md](entries/earth-taivel-arka-cheled.md) |
| חדל | chadal | **cease** | stopping because one cannot continue, by nature or by law (Rabbi Yosef Grayever); the halt comes from the person or thing itself, not from outside, and carries no verdict on whether it is right (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim) | [stopping-chadal-mana-chasach-kala-pasak.md](entries/stopping-chadal-mana-chasach-kala-pasak.md) |
| חדק | chedek | **brier** | a brier, behind the Rabbinic senses of cutting and pricking; chad plus dak, sharp and thin, or a metathesis of dochak, pressure (Ohalei Yehuda), which Ramban seems to follow | [thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md](entries/thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md) |

| חדש | chodesh | **month; new moon** | its primary sense is the *beginning* of the month, from chadash, "new," and "month" is only borrowed from there (Malbim, Rav Hirsch); Rav Hirsch adds that it names the month as an abstract unit of time | [month-chodesh-yerach.md](entries/month-chodesh-yerach.md) |
| חובב | | see entry | one of the *love* words | [love-ahavah-chibah.md](entries/love-ahavah-chibah.md) |

| חוג | chug | **circle, orbit** | what orbits around another body, as a planet does (Radak); a circle, or machug, considered from its center (Malbim); from Aramaic chinga, a circle dance, the nun dropped (Rabbi Klein, Rabbi Chelouche) | [around-saviv-heikef-afef-chug.md](entries/around-saviv-heikef-afef-chug.md) |

| חוח | choach | **thorn** | related to chach, a piece of jewelry fastened with a pin (Radak, Pappenheim), whose sharp point would recall a thorn | [thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md](entries/thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md) |
| חוט | chut | **thread, string** | the single thread out of which a fabric is woven or a garment sewn, and the thinnest word in the set, whence the Mishnaic chayat, tailor, and machat, needle; for Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim it is what repairs a deficiency (biliteral ח-ט, blemish) | [rope-chevel-chut-avot.md](entries/rope-chevel-chut-avot.md) |

| חולש | cholesh | **casting lots** | a rare word for casting lots, Nevuchadnetzar drawing lots each day over the nations (Shabbos 149b); tied to lachash, whisper, lots being cast in the quiet (Rabbi Shlomo HaAdani), or to chalash, weak, a lottery being weak proof of desert (Rabbi Yosef Yishai Rain); the unsettling uncertainty of chance (Kedushas Levi) | [lottery-goral-pur-payis-cholesh.md](entries/lottery-goral-pur-payis-cholesh.md) |
| חום | | see entry | one of the *red* words | [red-adom-shani-chamutz.md](entries/red-adom-shani-chamutz.md) |

| חומש | | see entry | one of the *armed* words | [armed-chamush-chalutz-mezuyan.md](entries/armed-chamush-chalutz-mezuyan.md) |

| חופש | chofesh | **free, released** | freedom from an obligation to work or serve (Wertheimer); the Tanach's other slave-freeing word; read against chafetz, desire, as negative liberty, the mere absence of coercion (Rabbi Jonathan Sacks) | [freedom-cheirus-chofesh-dror.md](entries/freedom-cheirus-chofesh-dror.md) |
| חוק | | see entry | one of the *law* words | [law-din-mishpat-chok-dat.md](entries/law-din-mishpat-chok-dat.md) |
| חור | | see entry | one of the *nose* words | [nose-af-chotem-nichirayim.md](entries/nose-af-chotem-nichirayim.md) |
| חורב | Chorev | **Horeb** | alluding to cherev, a sword, since the Sanhedrin's authority to carry out capital punishment comes from the Torah given there; a separate mountain from Sinai, or another peak of it (Shadal) | [sinai-chorev-gavnunim-bashan.md](entries/sinai-chorev-gavnunim-bashan.md) |
| חורבן | churban | **destruction** | the destruction of a built-up urban area, the milder of the pair (Malbim); a thing severed from what it needed to thrive, perhaps still standing (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); of the Beis HaMikdash, its spiritual disconnection through sin (Rabbi Klein) | [destruction-churban-shemamah.md](entries/destruction-churban-shemamah.md) |
| חורים | | see entry | one of the *freedom* words | [freedom-cheirus-chofesh-dror.md](entries/freedom-cheirus-chofesh-dror.md) |

| חותן | chosen | **father-in-law** | always a husband's father-in-law, never widened, since it names the man who made him a chasan (Pri Megadim); built on connection (Rav Hirsch); can also mean brother-in-law (Ibn Janach), which Radak disputes; any tie made by marriage (Benamozegh) | [in-laws-cham-chosen.md](entries/in-laws-cham-chosen.md) |
| חותנת | choseness | **mother-in-law** | always a husband's mother-in-law (Radak), formed from chosen, so it too never widened to a wife's, even in Mishnaic Hebrew (Pri Megadim) | [in-laws-cham-chosen.md](entries/in-laws-cham-chosen.md) |
| חזון | | see entry | one of the *prophet* words | [prophet-navi-roeh-chozeh.md](entries/prophet-navi-roeh-chozeh.md) |
| חזיז | chaziz | **thundercloud** | the cloud that comes with thunder, tied to sight because it flashes lightning (Pappenheim); from chazon, sight, or clouds sent as signs in Heaven (Chazal); colorful clouds (Sefer HaChochmah) | [clouds-anan-av-eid-nasi-chaziz.md](entries/clouds-anan-av-eid-nasi-chaziz.md) |
| חזק | chozek | **strong** | the standard word for strength, against above-normal ometz (Bedersi, Wertheimer); outer, physical strength (Vilna Gaon, Malbim); temporary strength that atrophies (Malbim to Yeshayahu 28:2); strength of will to enter danger (Shapira-Frankfurter); extra-strength koach that stands out, and the strength to withstand being overpowered, against tokef (Pappenheim) | [strength-koach-gevurah-ometz-chozek.md](entries/strength-koach-gevurah-ometz-chozek.md) |
| חזרה | chazarah | **turning back, reverting** | the about-face itself, turning back from where one now stands; Mishnaic, never in Tanach; the Targumim's word for going around (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur); getting out of the rut rather than the goal (Rabbi Klein) | [return-shuv-chazarah.md](entries/return-shuv-chazarah.md) |
| חטא | chet | **sin, inadvertent sin** | the general and lightest word; inadvertent (Gemara, Peirush HaRokeach); a lack, failing a positive mitzvah (Vilna Gaon); a goal missed (Rabbi Moshe Shapiro); knowingly indulging physical temptation (Malbim); alone, any sin (Rabbi Netanel Weil); the sins of youth, before the mind rules (Radak); also the punishment that follows (HaKsav VeHaKabbalah) | [sin-chet-avon-pesha.md](entries/sin-chet-avon-pesha.md) |
| חטיבה | | see entry | one of the *speech* words | [speech-dibbur-amirah.md](entries/speech-dibbur-amirah.md) |

| חיה | chayah | **wild animal** | the wild animal of uninhabited country (Ibn Ezra, Radak), favored by the Netziv; against that, the carnivore (Ramban), which the Netziv rejects from the deer and Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky defends, since a deer eats insects | [animal-behemah-chayah.md](entries/animal-behemah-chayah.md) |
| חיה | chayah | **wild animal** | from chai, an independent life-form not subservient to man (Rav Hirsch); see the separate entry on behemah and chayah | [beast-beir-behemah-baar-bur.md](entries/beast-beir-behemah-baar-bur.md) |
| חיה | chayah | **life-force** | the soul's transcendence, living on when the body dies (Bereishis Rabbah 14:9); the overall holistic life-force (the Vilna Gaon); the neshamah of the neshamah (Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin); not given to everyone, only after maturity and mitzvos (Rabbi Yaakov Yehoshua Falk) | [soul-nefesh-ruach-neshamah-chayah-yechidah.md](entries/soul-nefesh-ruach-neshamah-chayah-yechidah.md) |

| חיך | | see entry | one of the *licking* words | [licking-lechichah-lekikah.md](entries/licking-lechichah-lekikah.md) |

| חיל | cheil | **short wall** | a low wall running outside a taller one, with empty ground between them (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); a shorter wall inside the chomah (Rashi); Radak seems unsure which, and suggests a moat | [wall-chomah-kir-shur-kotel.md](entries/wall-chomah-kir-shur-kotel.md) |
| חילוני | chiloni | **stranger, non-Kohen** | the Targumim's frequent Aramaic for zar (Onkelos); in the Midrash a non-Kohen, as Scripture uses zar (Vayikra Rabbah 24:7); in Modern Hebrew a secular Jew | [stranger-zar-nachri-hedyot.md](entries/stranger-zar-nachri-hedyot.md) |
| חיץ | chayitz | **flimsy partition** | a flimsy partition (Rabbi Moshe Zacuto); a wall dividing one domain into two, equivalent to the Mishnaic mechitzah (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); a single appearance in Tanach, at Yechezkel 13:10 | [wall-chomah-kir-shur-kotel.md](entries/wall-chomah-kir-shur-kotel.md) |
| חירות | cheirus | **freedom** | the later, rabbinic word, freedom as a standing, the ben chorin; never freedom in Tanach; hooked by Avos 6:2 to charus, engraved on the Luchos; positive liberty, law studied until engraved on the heart (Rabbi Jonathan Sacks) | [freedom-cheirus-chofesh-dror.md](entries/freedom-cheirus-chofesh-dror.md) |
| חיתול | chitul | **wrap** | wrapping in soft fabric, as against tying tight (Malbim); in Modern Hebrew the noun is a diaper | [tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md](entries/tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md) |
| חכוי | chikui | **waiting** | waiting in full certainty, sure that it will happen and only waiting for it, the most certain of the three (Wertheimer) | [trust-bitachon-machseh-tikvah.md](entries/trust-bitachon-machseh-tikvah.md) |
| חכלילי | chachlilei | **bloodshot** | only of eyes reddened by drink; the reddened white ringing the iris (Rabbi Moshe Tedeschi-Ashkenazi); Ramban instead links it to kachol, blue | [red-adom-shani-chamutz.md](entries/red-adom-shani-chamutz.md) |
| חכם | | see entry | one of the *wisdom* words | [wisdom-chochmah-binah-daat-tevunah.md](entries/wisdom-chochmah-binah-daat-tevunah.md) |
| חכמה | chochmah | **wisdom** | what one hears and learns from others (Rashi, Radak, Chasam Sofer); mastery of any body of knowledge, in Tanach above all the sage's Torah (Bedersi); the unhurried learner who waits (Pappenheim); practical wisdom, truly only by revelation (Malbim); the lowest of the three | [wisdom-chochmah-binah-daat-tevunah.md](entries/wisdom-chochmah-binah-daat-tevunah.md) |

| חלב | | see entry | one of the *fat* words | [fat-cheilev-shuman-pader.md](entries/fat-cheilev-shuman-pader.md) |

| חלה |  | **** |  | [dough-arisah-batzek-issah.md](entries/dough-arisah-batzek-issah.md) |

| חלוץ | chalutz | **vanguard** | the units drawn out of the formation to serve at the front (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); men slipped off and separated from the nation (Malbim); armed at the loins (Ibn Ezra); removed from the nation as soldiers (Radak); shedding civilian clothing (Ibn Janach); equated with mezuyanim (Rashi) | [armed-chamush-chalutz-mezuyan.md](entries/armed-chamush-chalutz-mezuyan.md) |

| חליצה | chalitzah | **extracting, drawing out** | pulling something out of what envelops it, the foot from the shoe, a stone from a wall (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); by Shoresh Yesha, removing a shoe that must first be untied | [slipping-off-shemittah-chalitzah-shalaf.md](entries/slipping-off-shemittah-chalitzah-shalaf.md) |
| חלל | challal | **the slain, hollow** | literally empty or hollow, a body emptied of its soul like an emptied vessel; the root of chalil, chullin and a kohen's disqualified chalal; one killed by another man, where a meis died naturally (Rabbeinu Hillel) | [corpse-peger-neveilah-challal.md](entries/corpse-peger-neveilah-challal.md) |
| חלמיש | chalamish | **flint** | conventionally flint; a sub-category of tzur covering the very hardest stones, even diamond (Pappenheim); bound to tzur in construct, tzur hachalamish | [rock-tzur-chalamish.md](entries/rock-tzur-chalamish.md) |
| חלף | | see entry | one of the *exchange* words | [exchange-temurah-chalifah.md](entries/exchange-temurah-chalifah.md) |

| חם | cham | **father-in-law** | in Biblical Hebrew always a wife's father-in-law (Radak), widened in Mishnaic Hebrew to a husband's; from chomah, a wall around the bride (Rav Hirsch), or from heat, the warm love she receives (Pappenheim) | [in-laws-cham-chosen.md](entries/in-laws-cham-chosen.md) |
| חמדה | chemdah | **coveting** | desire for what is not itself a bodily pleasure, fine clothes, a house, money (Vilna Gaon); follows from the object's inherent, recognized properties (Pappenheim, Mecklenburg); roused by seeing it (Malbim); for what is not within reach (Shadal) | [desire-taavah-chemdah.md](entries/desire-taavah-chemdah.md) |

| טינוף | tinuf | **soiling** | soiling by what is not repulsive in itself but unwanted where it clings, ketchup on a shirt, the dirt secondary to the object (Pappenheim); plain soiling, without smell (Donash Ibn Labrat); synonymous with lichluch and zuhamah (Rabbi Tanchum HaYerushalmi) | [dirt-zuhamah-lichluch-tinuf-goal.md](entries/dirt-zuhamah-lichluch-tinuf-goal.md) |
| טירה | tirah | **fortress** | the defensive sense, an enclosed fort, perhaps a fortified village; the same as armon (Ibn Ezra); built of rows, from ט-ר (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim, Radak), or a fort built to guard (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim, Rabbi David Chaim Chelouche) | [palace-zvul-armon-apadna-tirah.md](entries/palace-zvul-armon-apadna-tirah.md) |

| טלה | tleh | **lamb** | another young sheep, and can name a young human, like English kid (Rav Hirsch); from tal, dew (Pappenheim); an animal still nursing (Rabbi Meir Mazuz); the female (the Rokeach) | [sheep-and-goats-seh-keves-ayil-eiz.md](entries/sheep-and-goats-seh-keves-ayil-eiz.md) |

| כעס | kaas | **anger** | the commonest, most generic term and the simplest, lowest grade (Pappenheim); anger pent up in the heart and never brought into action (Malbim); a metathesis of eches, poison in the heart (Rabbeinu Efrayim), or eches from kaas, a snake's venom released in anger (Rashi) | [anger-cheimah-ketzef-charon-rogez.md](entries/anger-cheimah-ketzef-charon-rogez.md) |

| כפות | kafut | **tied down** | Aramaic and Mishnaic tying down, glossed by Rashi sometimes with asirah and sometimes with keshirah; perhaps kin to kefiyah, compulsion, in line with Pappenheim's kaf-peh; or from a different Aramaic root (Dr. Michael Sokoloff) | [tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md](entries/tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md) |
| כפיפה | kefifah | **wicker basket** | Mishnaic, spelled sometimes with a kuf and sometimes with a kaf; seems to mean specifically a wicker basket (Shabbos 2:2; Sotah 2:1, 3:1; Keilim 26:1) | [basket-tene-sal-keluv.md](entries/basket-tene-sal-keluv.md) |
| כפיר | kfir | **young lion** | whoever sees it denies his own life (Rabbi Levi); an adolescent that denies his parents (Avos d'Rabbi Nasan); young but strong (Rashi); the cub whose teeth frighten (Vilna Gaon); less fierce, still too young to hunt (Rabbi Yechiel Michel Stern); a small, weak lion (Zohar) | [lion-aryeh-kfir-lavi-layish.md](entries/lion-aryeh-kfir-lavi-layish.md) |
| כפן | kafan | **dearth** | perhaps only the Aramaic for ra'av; famine from hoarding and high prices (Ralbag); food at hand that does not satisfy (Vilna Gaon); so starved he no longer feels hunger (Wertheimer); thirst, a minority view (Rabbi Moshe Zidel) | [famine-raav-kafan-batzores.md](entries/famine-raav-kafan-batzores.md) |
| כפרה | kapparah | **atonement** | every negative consequence of the sin wiped out (Rav Hirsch); a price paid for forgiveness, usually a korban, or a covering that hides the sin without removing it (Malbim); Mecklenburg and Wertheimer do not set it against the other two | [forgiveness-mechilah-selichah-kapparah.md](entries/forgiveness-mechilah-selichah-kapparah.md) |
| כפתור | | see entry | one of the *Egypt* words | [egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md](entries/egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md) |
| כר | kar | **swift camel / saddle-basket** | disputed; a fast-running camel (Ibn Ezra to Yeshayahu 16:1), a camel's saddle-basket (Ibn Ezra to Bereishis 31:34), or a young sheep (Rabbi Yosef Kimchi); a present (Niddah 31b, as Rashi reads it) | [camel-gamal-nakah-becher-kar.md](entries/camel-gamal-nakah-becher-kar.md) |
| כרגא | karga | **poll tax** | from Persian karaka or Arabic harag, a head tax, the fixed sum each individual was obligated to pay (see Rashi to Bava Metzia 73b); the same as gulgalta | [tax-mas-meches.md](entries/tax-mas-meches.md) |
| כרה | karah | **begin to dig, hollow out** | the first, preparatory stage of digging that does not finish the work (Malbim, Rav Hirsch); so even an unfinished pit brings liability (Malbim); a grave plot only marked out (Netziv); a hole meant to be closed, as a grave (Be'er Yitzchak) | [dig-karah-chafirah-chatzivah.md](entries/dig-karah-chafirah-chatzivah.md) |
| כרובים | kruvim | **cherubim** | the ninth rank; from Aramaic ravia, a lad, with a kaf of simile, so the kruvim on the Aron looked like children (Chagigah 13b, Sukkah 5b); also the destructive angels guarding the path to the Eitz HaChaim (Rashi); from rechev, what Hashem rides (Shadal) | [angel-classes-kruvim-chayos-ishim.md](entries/angel-classes-kruvim-chayos-ishim.md) |
| כרוספדין | kruspidin | **hem, fringe** | the Targum's Aramaic for both tzitzis and gedilim; a loanword from Greek kraspedon, the fringe or hem of a garment (Rabbi Binyamin Mussafia); Persian instead (Kohut) | [fringes-tzitzis-gedilim-petil.md](entries/fringes-tzitzis-gedilim-petil.md) |
| כרטיס | kartis | **card, document** | in the Yerushalmi (end of Kesubos ch. 9) one who lost his kartis writes another; karta in Arabic and la'az (Ramban) | [document-gett-shtar.md](entries/document-gett-shtar.md) |
| כריעה | kriah | **kneeling** | bowing on the knees (Megillah 22b, Berachos 34b); knees on the floor, then the face to the ground (Maharsha) | [bowing-kidah-kriah-hishtachavaah.md](entries/bowing-kidah-kriah-hishtachavaah.md) |
| כריתות | | see entry | one of the *excision* words | [excision-karet-ariri.md](entries/excision-karet-ariri.md) |
| כרכור | kirkur | **whirling, capering** | a specific act of dancing, the footwork; circular motion (Rabbi Yosef Kara), as young animals move in circles (Tedeschi-Ashkenazi); the movements of the feet, against mifazez of the hands (Rashbam) | [dancing-rikud-kirkur-pizuz.md](entries/dancing-rikud-kirkur-pizuz.md) |
| כרכרות | kirkaros | **swift beasts** | a prominent kind of camel (Ibn Ezra), any fast-running animal (Radak), or skipping young calves (Rabbi Yosef Bechor Shor) | [camel-gamal-nakah-becher-kar.md](entries/camel-gamal-nakah-becher-kar.md) |
| כרמלית | | see entry | one of the *widow* words | [widow-almanah-alman-armalta.md](entries/widow-almanah-alman-armalta.md) |
| כרפס |  | **** |  | [linen-sheish-bahd-butz-pishtim.md](entries/linen-sheish-bahd-butz-pishtim.md) |
| כרפס | karpas | **parsley, fabric** | one particular plant, parsley in the Yerushalmi, though the matter is far from settled (Rabbi Klein); in Esther a fabric, silk (Rabbi Saadia Gaon) or fine linen (Rabbi Dr. Ernest Klein), or a color, green (Radak) | [vegetable-yerek-yarok-karpas.md](entries/vegetable-yerek-yarok-karpas.md) |
| כרפסא | | see entry | one of the *vegetable and green* words | [vegetable-yerek-yarok-karpas.md](entries/vegetable-yerek-yarok-karpas.md) |
| כרת | kares | **cut, excise** | spiritual excision; a general word for cutting, whether or not it severs, as a sefer krisus (Pappenheim); also ratifying a covenant, once marked by cutting animals in half | [cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md](entries/cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md) |
| כרת | karet | **excision** | the sinner himself cut off; from the reunion of souls in the World to Come (Rabbi Yaakov Tzvi Mecklenburg), from the soul's Upper Source (Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin), or in body, soul or both (Ramban, Rabbeinu Bachya); Ibn Ezra adds the death of descendants | [excision-karet-ariri.md](entries/excision-karet-ariri.md) |
| כרתי | karti | **indigo dye** | the dye called Hindi, indis in Tosafos's Old French (Rabbeinu Yonah; Tosafos and Tosafos HaRosh to Chullin 47b); told apart from techeiles (Berachos 9b) | [blue-sapir-techeiles-kachol.md](entries/blue-sapir-techeiles-kachol.md) |
| כשב | kesev | **lamb** | an exact metathesis of keves with the same meaning (Radak, Ibn Ezra, Ibn Parchon), a bigger or older sheep (Baal HaTurim, Netziv), or a general term for sheep of any age (Malbim, Strashun) | [sheep-and-goats-seh-keves-ayil-eiz.md](entries/sheep-and-goats-seh-keves-ayil-eiz.md) |
| כשיל | kashil | **large axe** | a hapax at Tehillim 74:6; the bigger tool, which throws off scraps large enough that the one who commissioned the work keeps them (Mishnah Bava Kamma 10:10) | [cutting-tools-garzen-kardum-maatzad.md](entries/cutting-tools-garzen-kardum-maatzad.md) |
| כתב | ksav | **anything written** | anything written at all, the general term beside the more specific sefer, megillah, gilayon and iggeret (Malbim) | [book-sefer-iggeret-megillah.md](entries/book-sefer-iggeret-megillah.md) |
| כתיבה | ketivah | **writing** | the general, most common word, about 260 times in Tanach, used of the Luchos and of a Sefer Torah in ink on parchment; a worthy bearer of ideas that risks detaching part of the idea from the whole (Rav Hirsch) | [writing-ketivah-charut-chakuk.md](entries/writing-ketivah-charut-chakuk.md) |
| כתם | kesem | **fine gold** | gold so pure it can be beaten paper-thin (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim), which is why the same root gives ketem, a stain that stands out | [gold-zahav-paz-kesem-charutz.md](entries/gold-zahav-paz-kesem-charutz.md) |
| כתף | katef | **shoulder** | the shoulder as a whole (Ohel Moed), or its front (Rabbi Ezra Reuven Dangoor); at Iyov 31:22 it sits atop the shechem | [shoulder-shechem-katef.md](entries/shoulder-shechem-katef.md) |
| כתר | keter | **royal crown** | the crown of royalty, always keser malchus in Tanach; encircles the head without rising above it, a coronet (Malbim); some make it the general word; the sign of rule, worn by kings (Pappenheim); kingship (Rabbi Zev Leff) | [crown-keter-atarah-nezer.md](entries/crown-keter-atarah-nezer.md) |
| לא | lo | **you shall not** | the Torah's standard negation and the marker of a negative commandment; negates past fact and future command alike, you did not as well as you shall not (Rabbi Ber Oppenheimer); addressed concretely to a second person (Rabbi Aharon Maggid, as Rabbi Klein reads him) | [negation-lo-al-bal.md](entries/negation-lo-al-bal.md) |
| לאו | lav | **negative commandment** | simply a negative commandment, an anthimeria from lo, not; absent from Tanach and common in rabbinic writing; a prohibited act even where the punishment is not severe | [prohibition-azharah-issur-lav.md](entries/prohibition-azharah-issur-lav.md) |
| לאום | leom | **nation by religion, kingdom** | people joined by a shared religion, which can span several kingdoms (Malbim, from the Midrash); a family or clan within a larger nation (Edel), the word probably tied to em, mother | [nation-goy-am-leom-umah.md](entries/nation-goy-am-leom-umah.md) |
| לאלתר | le'alter | **on the spot** | a contraction of al atar, on the spot (Rabbi Yishaya Pick-Berlin, Rabbi Yaakov Emden), a word for place doing duty for time | [immediately-teikef-miyad-lealter-otyom.md](entries/immediately-teikef-miyad-lealter-otyom.md) |
| לאמר | | see entry | one of the *speech* words | [speech-dibbur-amirah.md](entries/speech-dibbur-amirah.md) |
| לאן | | see entry | one of the *where* words | [where-ayeh-eifoh-anah.md](entries/where-ayeh-eifoh-anah.md) |
| לב | lev | **heart, midst** | the heart, and by extension the midst of anything, since it sits roughly in the middle of the body, as the heart of the seas; whatever sits at the center or plays a central part (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim) | [middle-emtza-merkaz-lev-tabur.md](entries/middle-emtza-merkaz-lev-tabur.md) |
| לבוש | levush | **apparel, dress** | whatever one dresses in, of no set type, from lovesh; in usage the distinctive dress of a station, hence levush malchus; Shabbos 77b reads it lo bushah, "no shame" | [clothing-beged-levush-kesus-simlah.md](entries/clothing-beged-levush-kesus-simlah.md) |
| לביא | lavi | **lion, lioness** | its roar seizes men's hearts (Rabbi Levi), or it eats the heart first (Rabbi Menachem Azariah of Fano); younger than an ari (Baal HaTurim); after aryeh, before layish (Radak); a lioness that has borne young (Vilna Gaon); another species (Rabbi Yeshayah of Trani), a leopard (Pappenheim) | [lion-aryeh-kfir-lavi-layish.md](entries/lion-aryeh-kfir-lavi-layish.md) |
| לבלר | lavlar | **scribe** | the later loanword from Latin libellarius, not in Tanach; a general term taking in even the freelance clerk (Blau), or effectively synonymous with sofer, perhaps more formal (Krauss); Rashi defines each by the other | [scribe-sofer-lavlar.md](entries/scribe-sofer-lavlar.md) |
| לבן | lavan | **white** | seemingly the umbrella Hebrew term, covering every manifestation of white (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); the same root gives leveinah (brick), levanah (moon), levonah (frankincense) | [white-lavan-chivar-tzochar.md](entries/white-lavan-chivar-tzochar.md) |
| לבנה | leveinah | **brick** | the brick a man makes by mixing mortar, set against even, the stone formed by nature (Malbim); from even, built with in place of stones (Shadal) | [rock-even-sela.md](entries/rock-even-sela.md) |
| לבנה | levanah | **moon** | literally the white one, naming the moon by its perceived color (Rabbi Aharon Marcus); the source of Latin luna (Benamozegh) | [sun-and-moon-shemesh-chamah-yareach.md](entries/sun-and-moon-shemesh-chamah-yareach.md) |
| לברך | levarech | **to bless** | not blessing the Creator as He blesses man, which a mortal cannot do, but acknowledging Him as the source of all blessing (Rabbi Chaim Volozhiner); left out by Abudraham | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| להב | lahav | **flame, blade** | the flame that spurts outward from a larger fire, its outlet for spreading; hence also the blade of a knife or sword, the part that acts on things outside itself (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); not a bigger fire than aish | [fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md](entries/fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md) |
| להבה | | see entry | one of the *fire* words | [fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md](entries/fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md) |
| להבים | | see entry | one of the *Egypt* words | [egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md](entries/egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md) |
| להגיד | | see entry | one of the *telling* words | [telling-haggadah-sippur.md](entries/telling-haggadah-sippur.md) |
| להדר | lehader | **to beautify** | stressing the whole, the symmetrical and all-encompassing praiseworthiness in every aspect (Rabbi Shimshon Pincus); in Nusach Sefard followed by lenatzei'ach (Arizal) | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| להודות | lehodos | **to thank** | admitting that another did one a good turn and is owed gratitude; from hod, what lies beneath the surface, brought forward in words; set before lauding, since personal gratitude precedes the general duty to praise (Wertheimer) | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| להט | lahat | **blaze** | the fast movement of fire, spreading like wildfire; related to the root of bending; like lahav it can mean flame or blade, and is borrowed for enthusiasm | [fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md](entries/fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md) |
| להט | lahat | **sleight of hand, magic arts** | kishuf performed by the practitioner himself, named for the flash of a turning flame or blade (Sanhedrin 67b with Rashi; Ibn Ezra); its plain sense elsewhere is "flame" (Bereishis 3:24) | [magic-lahat-lat-ittim.md](entries/magic-lahat-lat-ittim.md) |
| להלל | lehallel | **to praise** | relaying another's virtue to a third party, as against thanking him for a good turn or dwelling on his good traits as such | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| לובים | | see entry | one of the *Egypt* words | [egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md](entries/egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md) |
| לודים | | see entry | one of the *Egypt* words | [egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md](entries/egypt-mitzrayim-patros-rahav.md) |
| לוז | luz | **almond, hazel** | almond, as in Arabic (Rabbi Saadia Gaon), and on Rabbi Klein's hedged upshot the Aramaic word for what shaked names in Hebrew; hazel (Rashi, Tosafos); the silverleaf poplar in another version of Rabbi Saadia Gaon; related to the cedar (Menachem Ibn Saruk); never Onkelos's rendering of shaked | [almond-luz-shaked.md](entries/almond-luz-shaked.md) |
| לוחם | | see entry | one of the *war* words | [war-milchamah-krav-pulmus.md](entries/war-milchamah-krav-pulmus.md) |
| לותיר | lotir | **Lothar, the Rhineland** | the Rishonim's own name for their region, from Lotharingia, the realm of Lothair II; Rabbi Yosef Prager argues it covered the whole Rhineland, Mainz, Worms and Speyer together | [germany-ashkenaz-germamia-lotir.md](entries/germany-ashkenaz-germamia-lotir.md) |
| לח | lach | **moist** | a little wet, not enough to wet what touches it, the inner moisture of every living thing (Pappenheim); equated with ratuv (Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Radak), and perhaps the native Hebrew against borrowed Aramaic (Rabbi Klein) | [wet-lach-ratuv-raanan.md](entries/wet-lach-ratuv-raanan.md) |
| לחיכה | lechichah | **lick away** | licking something less liquid, with a harder sound, as the ox licks the field bare (Rabbi Moshe Tedeschi-Ashkenazi); from cheich, the palate (Rabbi Yaakov Berger, Rabbi Zilberberg); eating quickly (Ibn Parchon); Ibn Saruk and Radak define it by lekikah; Chazal extend it to fire | [licking-lechichah-lekikah.md](entries/licking-lechichah-lekikah.md) |
| לחם | lechem | **bread** | the wide word, over three hundred times in Tanach; the staple food of a society, so meat in Arabic (Rabbi Dr. Guy Matalon); from soldering, food cementing body and soul (Netziv); what sustains a person's inner moisture (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim) | [bread-lechem-kikar-challah-pat.md](entries/bread-lechem-kikar-challah-pat.md) |
| לחץ | lachatz | **pressure** | the eye on the one applying the pressure, saying nothing of whether it worked (Schwab); not necessarily nefarious, pressure to extract a benefit (Ashkenazi), against pressuring chiefly to make a man suffer (Pappenheim); physical or psychological (Posen) | [pressure-lachatz-dchak-negisah-atz.md](entries/pressure-lachatz-dchak-negisah-atz.md) |
| לט | lat | **secret arts** | the concealed, undercover method, adjuring sheidim to act on one's behalf (Sanhedrin 67b with Rashi; Ramban from ל-ט, "clandestine") | [magic-lahat-lat-ittim.md](entries/magic-lahat-lat-ittim.md) |
| לילית | lilis | **female demon** | a *sheidah*, whether the name of one particular demoness, mother of all the *sheidim* and consort of Samael (the *Zohar*), or the name of a class of them; at Yeshayahu 34:14 a female demon (Rashi), a night bird (Ibn Ezra) or a night animal (Radak), as Rabbi Tanchum HaYerushalmi has it, a wild animal that scavenges by night; from yelel, howling (Chemdas HaChemdah) | [demon-sheid-lilis-ruach.md](entries/demon-sheid-lilis-ruach.md) |
| לילך | lilach | **purple, lilac** | also modern, the lilac flower's name extended to the color, as with the modern words for lavender and mauve | [purple-argaman-segol-lilach.md](entries/purple-argaman-segol-lilach.md) |
| לינה | linah | **staying overnight** | technically leaving something overnight rather than sleeping, so it governs sacrificial meat, unpaid wages and a hanging body as readily as a guest; tied to laylah (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); the time for sleeping (Rabbi Yosef Nechemias) | [sleep-sheinah-tardeimah-tenumah.md](entries/sleep-sheinah-tardeimah-tenumah.md) |
| ליש | layish | **old lion, lioness** | its teeth knead a man's skin like dough (Rabbi Levi); the last and strongest stage (Radak); a lioness that has not yet borne young (Vilna Gaon); a leopard (Rabbi Pinchas Eliyahu Horowitz) | [lion-aryeh-kfir-lavi-layish.md](entries/lion-aryeh-kfir-lavi-layish.md) |
| לכלוך | lichluch | **grime** | post-biblical; dirtying by something not disgusting in itself but unwanted where it landed (Pappenheim); wet, kin to lichluach (Kohut), so no chatzitzah (Mikvaos 9:4); equated with tinuf by Ibn Janach and Radak | [dirt-zuhamah-lichluch-tinuf-goal.md](entries/dirt-zuhamah-lichluch-tinuf-goal.md) |
| למה | lamah | **why, for what purpose** | seen as la- ("for") plus mah ("what"), so it asks toward what end; Mecklenburg and Malbim make it the question of ultimate purpose, and Rabbi Wertheimer hears complaint or rebuke in it | [why-lamah-madua.md](entries/why-lamah-madua.md) |
| למואל | Lemuel | **Lemuel** | at Mishlei 31:1 (Lemoel at 31:4); nam la'El, he spoke to Hashem (the Midrash), the commentaries explaining NUN turning to LAMED as dentals do; against the positive readings of Ibn Ezra, Ralbag and Rashi | [names-shlomo-koheles-agur-lemuel.md](entries/names-shlomo-koheles-agur-lemuel.md) |
| למוד | limmud | **teaching by drilling** | going over the lesson again and again until it is engraved on the pupil's heart (Shadal, cited by Malbim); bringing the teaching to its conclusion, seeing the seeds to fruition (Rav Hirsch); runs both ways, the student teaching too (Rabbi Klein) | [teaching-horaah-limmud-alef.md](entries/teaching-horaah-limmud-alef.md) |
| לנצח | | see entry | one of the *praise* words | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| לסטים | listim | **robber, brigand** | a Greek loanword for a robber; whether an armed listim, who takes openly yet carries a weapon for fear of being caught, is a ganav or a gazlan is disputed (Kesef Mishneh, Lechem Mishneh, Even HaAzel) | [theft-genevah-gezeilah-chamas.md](entries/theft-genevah-gezeilah-chamas.md) |
| לספר | | see entry | one of the *telling* words | [telling-haggadah-sippur.md](entries/telling-haggadah-sippur.md) |
| לע | | see entry | one of the *worm* words | [worm-rimah-toleah.md](entries/worm-rimah-toleah.md) |
| לעיסה | | see entry | one of the *chewing* words | [chew-koses-loes.md](entries/chew-koses-loes.md) |
| לעלה | le'aleh | **to raise high** | raising Hashem's standing by admitting that He is above everything, as against leromem, above us (Rabbi Shimshon Pincus) | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| לענה | la'anah | **wormwood** | very bitter but not said to be deadly (Rashi, Radak); counted a synonym of rosh, chamat and ra'al, all poison, by Rabbi Shlomo of Urbino, which is quite novel | [poison-eres-rosh-chamat-sam-hamaves.md](entries/poison-eres-rosh-chamat-sam-hamaves.md) |
| לעס | lo'es | **chew** | rabbinic, apparently a loanword from Aramaic; equated with koses (Rashi); ordinary chewing toward swallowing (Rabbi Meir Mazuz); the more workaday chew (Rabbi Yitzchak Barda); perhaps different only in language of origin (Rabbi Reuven Chaim Klein) | [chew-koses-loes.md](entries/chew-koses-loes.md) |
| לפאר | lefa'er | **to glorify** | fixing on one specific praiseworthy aspect, as against lehader, which stresses the whole (Rabbi Shimshon Pincus) | [praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md](entries/praise-hallel-shevach-hodaah-kilus.md) |
| לפיד | lapid | **torch** | used when the focus is the object carrying the fire rather than the fire itself; Radak reads aish pladot as another way of saying lapid aish | [fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md](entries/fire-aish-lehavah-shalheves-lapid.md) |

| סודר | sudar | **shawl** | the Talmud's term for a shawl worn by a man, as against the woman's tza'if and redid; also a cloth waved as a signal; from the Greek soudarion and Latin sudarium (Rabbi Ernest Klein) | [veil-tzaif-redid.md](entries/veil-tzaif-redid.md) |
| סוחר | socher | **merchant, wholesaler** | the general Biblical word; a wholesaler who buys in bulk and supplies the rochel (Malbim to Yechezkel 27:3), and who travels from town to town (Rashi to Eruvin 55a) | [merchant-socher-rochel-cnaani-tagar.md](entries/merchant-socher-rochel-cnaani-tagar.md) |

| סולם | sulam | **ladder** | a ladder, though Rashi defines it by maalos and madreigos alike; perhaps moveable or nearer vertical than a stair; cognate of Akkadian simmiltu, stairway (Tawil, Landsberger), or from ס-ל-ל, a paved path up (Rav Hirsch, Gesenius), or from ע-ל, the root of maalos (Rabbi Aharon Marcus) | [level-madreigah-maalah-sulam.md](entries/level-madreigah-maalah-sulam.md) |
| סולת | soles | **fine flour** | the sifted, refined grade made of the endosperm alone (Rav Hirsch), better than kemach (Rashi); always wheat flour (Rashi, Rashbam), though Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim objects that soles alone does not fix the species | [flour-kemach-soles.md](entries/flour-kemach-soles.md) |
| סומא | suma | **blind man** | the Aramaic of the Gemara and Targumim; it shares its root with Samael, the Zohar's name for the Angel of Death, who for Rabbi Mordechai HaKohen of Tzfas is in himself blind | [blindness-iver-suma-sagi-nahor-sanverim.md](entries/blindness-iver-suma-sagi-nahor-sanverim.md) |
| סומק | sumak | **red (Aramaic)** | the plain Talmudic Aramaic red, and the Targumim's word for adom and chachlilei (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur, Meturgeman) | [red-adom-shani-chamutz.md](entries/red-adom-shani-chamutz.md) |
| סוס | sus | **horse** | the general word, some 140 times in Tanach; root linked to sasson, gladness, the horse being the liveliest and happiest of animals (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim, Rav Hirsch, Tzror HaMor) | [horse-sus-rechesh-achashtranim.md](entries/horse-sus-rechesh-achashtranim.md) |
| סוף | suf | **reeds** | the reed growing in a marsh, hence Yam Suf, the Sea of Reeds; Rashi only associates it with agam and renders it roisel, the common reed (Rabbi Avraham Meir HaKohen Glanzer) | [marsh-achu-agam-bitzah.md](entries/marsh-achu-agam-bitzah.md) |
| סופר | sofer | **scribe** | the Hebrew word, in Tanach and the Mishnah, one who produces a sefer, grown from counting (Dougherty); an official scribe in a bureaucratic post (Blau), though Krauss holds it the same as lavlar; plural sofrim often the early Sages | [scribe-sofer-lavlar.md](entries/scribe-sofer-lavlar.md) |
| סופרים | | see entry | one of the *scribe* words | [scribe-sofer-lavlar.md](entries/scribe-sofer-lavlar.md) |

| סלה | selah | **forever** | "disputed: forever, without end (Rashi, Meiri), the ever-repeating continual (Wertheimer); an interjection closing an idea (Radak, Malbim), a pause to take it in (Rabbi Chaim Friedlander); an affirmation, so it is (Ibn Ezra); a cue to beat a basket-shaped drum, from sal (some scholars)" | [forever-olam-netzach-selah-vaed.md](entries/forever-olam-netzach-selah-vaed.md) |
| סלון | salon | **thorn, thistle** | thorns at Yechezkel 2:6 and 28:24 (Rashi, Mahari Kara); Pappenheim splits them, salonim the people who repeatedly provoke, silon the thistle that stabs again and again | [thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md](entries/thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md) |
| סלונים | | see entry | one of the *refusal* words | [refusal-miun-siruv.md](entries/refusal-miun-siruv.md) |
| סליחה | selichah | **forgiveness** | forgiveness proper, the bond between the sinner and the One sinned against mended (Rav Hirsch); the Biblical word; reaches the whole sin but only defers its punishment (Mecklenburg); a reprieve, time to repay slowly (Wertheimer); deferring the debt (Rabbi Dosa the Greek); restoring the love that stood before the sin (Rabbi Zev Hoberman); forgiving the infraction itself, said with chet (Rabbi Eliyahu Menachem Margulies, after the Vilna Gaon) | [forgiveness-mechilah-selichah-kapparah.md](entries/forgiveness-mechilah-selichah-kapparah.md) |
| סלע | sela | **sela** | the Mishnaic name for exactly what Tanach calls a shekel (Yerushalmi Kiddushin 1:3; Rashi, Rambam, Sefer HaChinuch); its other Mishnaic sense is still "rock" | [coins-shekel-sela-beka-darkemon.md](entries/coins-shekel-sela-beka-darkemon.md) |
| סלע | sela | **crag** | a hard rock fixed in the ground, often a rocky height, and later a coin; attached to the ground (Rabbi Immanuel Chai Ricci); harder calcite-bound rock whose pieces fly outward (Pappenheim); rising up out of the ground (Rabbi Aharon Marcus) | [rock-even-sela.md](entries/rock-even-sela.md) |

| סנה | sneh | **thornbush** | the Burning Bush, a thorn bush (Rashi, Rabbi Saadia Gaon); a messy bush in which every kind of thorn grows, from ס-ן, disorder (Pappenheim); thorns like sharp teeth, from ש-ן (Rabbi David Chaim Chelouche) | [thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md](entries/thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md) |

| סעודה | seudah | **meal** | a meal generally associated with bread, from saad, to sustain (Radak), named for what it does for the body; the word for the three Shabbos meals; centers on eating, against mishteh (Rabbi Tzaddok HaKohen of Lublin); the heavier afternoon meal, against the evening mishteh (Shadal) | [meal-seudah-mishteh-mesibah.md](entries/meal-seudah-mishteh-mesibah.md) |

| עד | eid | **witness** | the Hebrew word; one who was present and so knows (Rabbi Shlomo Aharon Wertheimer), whose testimony ties the deed to the doer (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); it carries a second sense of "warn" | [witness-eid-sahad.md](entries/witness-eid-sahad.md) |
| עדה | eidah | **congregation** | a body joined for a stated purpose (Rabbi Avraham Bedersi); the Vilna Gaon, a gathering of the righteous | [gathering-asifah-kovetz-kehillah-agur.md](entries/gathering-asifah-kovetz-kehillah-agur.md) |
| עדות | eidus | **testimony** | what the eid gives; also a class of mitzvos that testify to what happened to Klal Yisrael, and a name for the Torah itself, which warns (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim) | [witness-eid-sahad.md](entries/witness-eid-sahad.md) |
| עדי | | see entry | one of the *spoils of war* words | [spoils-shalal-bizah-malkoach.md](entries/spoils-shalal-bizah-malkoach.md) |
| עדין | | see entry | one of the *pleasure* words | [pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md](entries/pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md) |
| עדן | eden | **sensual pleasure, delight of the senses** | pleasure of the body and the five senses, in Tanach almost always of taste and touch; it joins the one enjoying to the object, from ע-ד (Pappenheim), and stays physical even when it yields spiritual pleasure; from idan, time (Rabbi Nissim of Marseilles) | [pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md](entries/pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md) |
| עדנה | | see entry | one of the *pleasure* words | [pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md](entries/pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md) |
| עוגה | ugah | **cake, flat round loaf** | round is the word's core sense, not the baking; Choni draws his circle with ug ugah (Taanis 23a), and an ugah shel mayim is a round water pit (Rashi to Chullin 41a); Dr. Tamar Katzir and Rabbi Shaul Goldman suggest it is flat and two-dimensional, against the spherical kikar | [cake-ugah-chararah-gluskos.md](entries/cake-ugah-chararah-gluskos.md) |
| עולל | olel | **toddler** | from ע-ל, on top, hence the weaned child who now gets himself up to seek food (Pappenheim); the earliest of the ע-ל stages, before elem | [child-yeled-olel-roveh-ravya.md](entries/child-yeled-olel-roveh-ravya.md) |

| עונג | oneg | **delight, enjoyment** | pleasure of the soul, mind and heart, even when it arrives by way of the body, as oneg Shabbos (Pappenheim); for Rav Hirsch, being surrounded by favorable conditions, like anak, a necklace | [pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md](entries/pleasure-oneg-eden-pinuk.md) |

| עז | oz | **might** | strength of spirit, a resolve others cannot deter, visible in the face (Wertheimer); the stable and unwavering, whence azus, brazenness (Pappenheim); primarily Divine, supernatural power, against gevurah (Wessely, Rabbi Edel); tied to otzem and eitz, strong or hard (Rabbi Aharon Marcus) | [strength-koach-gevurah-ometz-chozek.md](entries/strength-koach-gevurah-ometz-chozek.md) |

| עין | ein | **color** | construct of ayin, eye; the one specific color of a thing, since the eye is the instrument that tells colors apart (Raavad I, Emunah HaRamah); Rambam uses it for color in some cases, and tzeva in others | [color-tzeva-gavan-ein-mareh.md](entries/color-tzeva-gavan-ein-mareh.md) |
| עינוי | inui | **affliction** | the Torah's own term for what is required on Yom Kippur (Vayikra 23:27 to 32, Bamidbar 29:7), of which not eating and drinking is one part | [fasting-tzom-taanis.md](entries/fasting-tzom-taanis.md) |
| עיסה | issah | **kneaded dough** | the Mishnah's word, absent from Tanach as dough; what must be kneaded and so is squeezed and trampled (Pappenheim, Mecklenburg, Marcus); the same word as arisah without the extra reish (Rabbi Baruch HaLevi Epstein) | [dough-arisah-batzek-issah.md](entries/dough-arisah-batzek-issah.md) |
| עיף | ayef | **tired, weary** | tired with something still left in him (Rabbi Shimon Schwab); worn down by continuous repeated action (Rabbi Yosef of Saragossa) or the regular tiredness of one with naturally low energy (Malbim). For Rabbi Shlomo Aharon Wertheimer, fatigue to the point of fainting, and hence also "thirsty" | [tired-ayef-yaef-yagea.md](entries/tired-ayef-yaef-yagea.md) |

| עיר | ayir | **foal** | the young one, her offspring where paired with aton; the young of a chamor or of a pere (Radak); the adolescent donkey whose strength is being revealed (Pappenheim); a young horse in rabbinic usage (Rashi) | [donkey-chamor-aton-pere-ayir-pered.md](entries/donkey-chamor-aton-pere-ayir-pered.md) |

| עירוב | iruv | **mixing, intermingling** | the mixing up of dry objects, as with people intermingling (Rabbi Shimon Dov Ber Analak of Shidlitz), like Ezra's hisarvu of Jewish seed with the nations and Tehillim's vayisarvu with the gentiles | [mixing-iruv-mizug-dimua.md](entries/mixing-iruv-mizug-dimua.md) |

| עלם | elem | **young man** | "tied to ne'elam, hidden: potential still undeveloped (Rav Hirsch); one who hides his words, a sign of wisdom (Rabbeinu Efrayim); sheer strength (Rabbi Analak); physical maturity against naar's intellectual and spiritual (Mecklenburg, summarizing Pappenheim)" | [youth-naar-almah-elem.md](entries/youth-naar-almah-elem.md) |

| צפעוני | tzifoni | **viper** | an evil snake, set against the completely evil efeh (Rashi); Radak holds tzifoni and efeh are two words for the same creature | [snake-nachash-saraph-tanin-peten.md](entries/snake-nachash-saraph-tanin-peten.md) |
| צפצוף | tziftzuf | **chirping, prattle** | the bird's sound, the voice of its anticipation (Pappenheim); by extension a low rapid whisper, or babble meant to be audible but almost always unintelligible (Rabbi Shaul Goldman), the prattle of lashon hara (Rashi, Ramban); in the Rema's halachic usage, simply to whistle | [whistle-shreikah-tziftzuf.md](entries/whistle-shreikah-tziftzuf.md) |
| צפרא |  | **** |  | [bird-of-tzipor-kanaf.md](entries/bird-of-tzipor-kanaf.md) |
| צפרא | tzafra | **morning** | the standard Aramaic for morning; Onkelos gives it for both shachar and boker in Chumash, while in Iyov, Mishlei and Tehillim the Targum keeps it for boker alone (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur); linked with tzipor, bird, though which came first is disputed (Ramban, Rabbi Aharon Marcus) | [morning-shachar-boker-tzafra.md](entries/morning-shachar-boker-tzafra.md) |
| צפרדע | | see entry | one of the *plague* words | [plague-dever-mageifah-negef.md](entries/plague-dever-mageifah-negef.md) |
| צר | tzar | **adversary, persecutor** | the overt enemy, hating with such heat that he attacks openly and spends his own reputation and resources to do it; Haman is tzorer haYehudim | [enemy-oyev-soneh-tzar.md](entries/enemy-oyev-soneh-tzar.md) |
| צרוע | tzarua | **leper (while afflicted)** | the man while the affliction is actually on him (Rabbi Eliezer Perlmutter, Even Moshe); for Shadal, one who has only a single nega, a distinction Rabbi Klein calls hard to substantiate | [leprosy-tzaraas-nega-metzora.md](entries/leprosy-tzaraas-nega-metzora.md) |
| צרור | tzror | **binding tight** | a union of strongly connected parts, from tzadi-reish (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); money tied up in the hand, and tzaros, co-wives tied together by marriage to one man | [tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md](entries/tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md) |
| צרי | tzari | **balm, balsam** | a scented potion used medicinally, the balsam resin of Tanach and the ketores (Rambam, Bereishis Rabbah) or theriaca (Rashi); what drips from the ketaf tree (Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel), or on Ramban's reading of Rambam a piece of the tree itself | [balsam-panag-tzari-afarsemon.md](entries/balsam-panag-tzari-afarsemon.md) |
| צרעה | | see entry | one of the *leprosy* words | [leprosy-tzaraas-nega-metzora.md](entries/leprosy-tzaraas-nega-metzora.md) |
| צרעת | tzaraas | **leprosy, the affliction itself** | the impurity that clings to the person because of sin (Arizal, Shaar HaMitzvos); Ibn Ezra reads it as "disease" in a general sense | [leprosy-tzaraas-nega-metzora.md](entries/leprosy-tzaraas-nega-metzora.md) |
| קבה | kavah | **public curse** | a general curse on a man and all that is his, uttered in public with his name stated explicitly, which arur does not connote (Malbim) | [curse-arur-kelalah-allah-kavah.md](entries/curse-arur-kelalah-allah-kavah.md) |
| קבץ | kovetz | **collecting** | gathering without necessarily bringing in (Malbim), or arranging into one place what is already inside (Vilna Gaon); Radak, gathering what is far-flung; Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim, gathering piece by piece | [gathering-asifah-kovetz-kehillah-agur.md](entries/gathering-asifah-kovetz-kehillah-agur.md) |
| קדוש | kadosh | **martyr, holy one** | the Jewish term for one killed al kiddush Hashem, from "holy," never from "witness" as the Syriac and Arabic terms for martyr are | [witness-eid-sahad.md](entries/witness-eid-sahad.md) |
| קדישין | kadishin | **holy ones** | not on Rambam's list; holy and set apart in that they do not carry out decrees themselves but tell the other angels what to do (the school of the Rokeach) | [angel-classes-kruvim-chayos-ishim.md](entries/angel-classes-kruvim-chayos-ishim.md) |
| קדם | kedem | **before, east** | before in time, with mukdam, kadmon and hakdamah; spatially east, where the sun rises and so what comes first; Targum Onkelos renders b'reishis as b'kadmin; from kuf-dalet, read with kodkod, the skull (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim) | [beginning-reishis-techilah-kedem.md](entries/beginning-reishis-techilah-kedem.md) |
| קדם | kedem | **east, forward side** | from kodem, early or forward, pointing to the rising sun first shining from the east; the word also carries time, so check whether a pasuk means eastward or aforetime | [directions-tzafon-darom-mizrach-maarav.md](entries/directions-tzafon-darom-mizrach-maarav.md) |
| קהילה | kehillah | **assembly** | any gathering of people, and of people only, never animals or objects (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); tied to kol, a sound summoning them | [gathering-asifah-kovetz-kehillah-agur.md](entries/gathering-asifah-kovetz-kehillah-agur.md) |
| קהל | Yom HaKahal | **Day of the Congregation** | Devarim 18:16, the Torah's name for the day of Matan Torah, and the ground for reading Atzeres as gathering (Rabbi Dovid Tzvi Hoffmann) | [shavuos-atzeres-katzir-bikkurim.md](entries/shavuos-atzeres-katzir-bikkurim.md) |
| קהלת | Koheles | **Koheles** | from hakhel and kahal, because his teachings were said in gatherings, "then Shlomo gathered" (Melachim I 8:1), or because he gathered up many kinds of wisdom (Rashi to Koheles 1:1); a common noun, given hakoheles (Ibn Ezra) | [names-shlomo-koheles-agur-lemuel.md](entries/names-shlomo-koheles-agur-lemuel.md) |

| קונטרס | kuntres | **pamphlet** | a short treatise not weighty enough to stand as its own sefer; the Tosafists' name for Rashi's Gemara commentary; from the Greek (Rabbi Binyamin Mussafia, Rabbi Ernest Klein, Rabbi Daniel Sperber) or from the Latin quinternus, a quire (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur) | [book-sefer-iggeret-megillah.md](entries/book-sefer-iggeret-megillah.md) |
| קונם | | see entry | one of the *vow* words | [vow-neder-shevuah-nedavah.md](entries/vow-neder-shevuah-nedavah.md) |
| קוץ | kotz | **thorn** | the thorn, named for its many sharp ends, from ק-ץ, the end of a thing (Pappenheim) | [thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md](entries/thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md) |
| קור | kor | **bitter cold, freezing** | the severe cold that hurts, felt on the coldest winter days or in touching cold metal, from the root of strong impact (Pappenheim); the drop in temperature itself (Rabbi Yehoshua Steinberg) | [cold-kor-tzinah.md](entries/cold-kor-tzinah.md) |
| קורנס | kurnas | **smith's hammer** | Mishnaic only, the hammer that beat the Menorah from one block of gold (Rashi to Shemos 25:31); "a big makeves" (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur) or "a small makeves" (Sefer HeAruch) | [hammer-makevet-patish-kurnas.md](entries/hammer-makevet-patish-kurnas.md) |
| קושיא | | see entry | one of the *hard* words | [hard-kashah-kashiach-perech.md](entries/hard-kashah-kashiach-perech.md) |
| קטב | ketev | **cut into** | a cut that slices into the thickness without severing through, like a paper cut; in Tanach always an illness that cuts the innards | [cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md](entries/cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md) |
| קטגור | kategor | **accuser, prosecutor** | Greek kata plus agora, one who speaks against another before an assembly; a slanderer or informer (Rabbeinu Chananel, Rambam, Rashbatz, Rabbi Yaakov bar Shimshon); ketata plus tigra (Machzor Vitri); antonym of praklit in Avos 4:11 and of sanegor elsewhere | [advocate-meilitz-praklit-sanegor.md](entries/advocate-meilitz-praklit-sanegor.md) |
| קטילה | ketilah | **killing (Aramaic)** | the Targumim's word for both Hebrew terms, and the ordinary Aramaic verb; in Hebrew Rabbi Pappenheim limits it to striking a man to the verge of death, and its Talmudic sense of "cutting" may, Rabbi Klein suggests, be its core | [murder-retzichah-harigah-ketilah.md](entries/murder-retzichah-harigah-ketilah.md) |
| קטיפה | ketifah | **pluck** | severing what was only flimsily attached, the word for plucking a flower | [cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md](entries/cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md) |
| קטירה | ketirah | **tie** | the Aramaic of keshirah and Targum's standard rendering of it (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur), by a shin-to-tav shift (Rabbi Yaakov Berger); in Hebrew the root is smoke or incense; Rabbinic katir can mean a conspiracy | [tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md](entries/tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md) |
| קטף | ketaf | **balsam tree** | the tree from which tzari drips (Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel), glossed as the balsam tree (Rambam); Onkelos's rendering of both tzari and nataf, naming the tree where nataf names the manner | [balsam-panag-tzari-afarsemon.md](entries/balsam-panag-tzari-afarsemon.md) |

| קידושין | kiddushin | **betrothal** | the Mishnah's term for the same act; from hekdesh, forbidding her to all others (Rabbanan Savorai), a rabbinic term because only the rabbinic enactment makes her like hekdesh (Rabbi Shor, Rabbi Horowitz); from designating, not consecrating (Tosafos); a loanword from Greek ekdosis (Satlow), which Rabbi Klein finds hard to accept; a fence against sin, and so kedushah (Hon Ashir) | [betrothal-erusin-kiddushin-nissuin.md](entries/betrothal-erusin-kiddushin-nissuin.md) |

| קימוש | kimosh | **thorn** | the thorn that grows along a field's perimeter, against the ordinary charul (Vilna Gaon) | [thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md](entries/thorns-kotz-dardar-sneh-charul.md) |
| קינוח | kinuach | **wiping** | Rabbinic only; cleaning by wiping off what soils, an expression of finality, what is wiped away gone for good (Rashi) | [washing-kevisah-rechitzah-shetifah-hadachah.md](entries/washing-kevisah-rechitzah-shetifah-hadachah.md) |

| קלון | kalon | **dishonor, disgrace** | from kal, light; declaring a man a lightweight, worth less than he is and not worth the honor due him, lowering a value where bizayon cancels it (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim) | [disgrace-bizayon-kalon-zilzul-gnai.md](entries/disgrace-bizayon-kalon-zilzul-gnai.md) |

| קלמתא | kalmta | **lice (Aramaic)** | the Targum's word for kinnim (Onkelos and Targum Yonasan to Shemos 8:12 to 14); the Gemara's form is kalmei (Berachos 51b, Niddah 20b), which Rashi identifies with it | [lice-kinnim-kalmta-parosh.md](entries/lice-kinnim-kalmta-parosh.md) |

| קמה | | see entry | one of the *flour* words | [flour-kemach-soles.md](entries/flour-kemach-soles.md) |

| קמיצה | | see entry | one of the *miser* words | [miser-kilay-tzaykan-kamtzan.md](entries/miser-kilay-tzaykan-kamtzan.md) |

| קן | | see entry | one of the *garden* words | [garden-gan-pardes-bustan.md](entries/garden-gan-pardes-bustan.md) |

| קנה | kaneh | **reed, stem, tube** | a pipe-like item, typically hollow in the middle, rather than a container; for Rabbi Reuven Chaim Klein hollowness characterizes it, and Rashbam and Ibn Ezra write that the Menorah's kanim ought to be hollow | [vessel-pach-kankan-kad-chavis.md](entries/vessel-pach-kankan-kad-chavis.md) |

| קנקן | kankan | **jug, jar** | absent from Tanach, Mishnaic only; typically a pottery vessel (Tosafot to Avodah Zarah 32a) used for wine, oil or water; a loanword from Latin canna, probably by reduplication (Kohut), the Latin itself from Hebrew kaneh (Rabbi Ernest Klein), whence, Rabbi Reuven Chaim Klein infers, its hollow receptacle | [vessel-pach-kankan-kad-chavis.md](entries/vessel-pach-kankan-kad-chavis.md) |
| קסקס | | see entry | one of the *chewing* words | [chew-koses-loes.md](entries/chew-koses-loes.md) |
| קפיצה | kefitzah | **leaping** | both feet leave the ground (Vilna Gaon); covering several steps in one to arrive faster, not avoiding what lies underneath (Pappenheim); hence kefitzas haderech, and anything done in haste | [jumping-pesach-dilug-kefitzah.md](entries/jumping-pesach-dilug-kefitzah.md) |

| קציר | Chag HaKatzir | **Festival of the Harvest** | Shemos 23:16; Shavuos falls in the grain harvest, wheat in particular, and the grain harvest ran exactly seven weeks (Rashi to Yirmiyahu 5:24) | [shavuos-atzeres-katzir-bikkurim.md](entries/shavuos-atzeres-katzir-bikkurim.md) |
| קצף | ketzef | **rage** | anger at the boil, the word also naming the bubbles of boiling water (Ibn Ezra, Radak); visible in the sweat on the face (Rokeach); the most extreme form (Eitz Yosef); outward anger coolly formulated by the intellect, even for a third party (Malbim); foam at the lips (Pappenheim) | [anger-cheimah-ketzef-charon-rogez.md](entries/anger-cheimah-ketzef-charon-rogez.md) |
| קר | | see entry | one of the *cold* words | [cold-kor-tzinah.md](entries/cold-kor-tzinah.md) |

| קרדם | kardum | **adze-axe, mattock** | seemingly a double-headed tool, an adze blade on one side of the head and an axe blade on the other (as Mishnah Keilim 13:3 suggests, and so Radak for the Biblical tool too), against Ibn Janach who defines it "spade" | [cutting-tools-garzen-kardum-maatzad.md](entries/cutting-tools-garzen-kardum-maatzad.md) |
| קרי | keri | **offhandedness, flippancy** | in Vayikra 26, serving Hashem in a glib, non-deliberate way, answered in kind (Rav Hirsch), or the sinner's antagonistic posture meant to anger Hashem (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim); in the Mishnah, a seminal emission | [chance-mikreh-keri-teunah-irua.md](entries/chance-mikreh-keri-teunah-irua.md) |
| קריעה | korea | **tear** | tearing something soft that comes apart easily, whence kriah (Pappenheim); ripping apart what was once separate (Shulchan Aruch HaRav), hence kriyas Yam Suf (Rabbi Yitzchok Meir Alter of Ger); acted upon from outside (Rabbi Shmuel Borenstein of Sochatchov) | [cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md](entries/cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md) |
| קריצתא | kritzuta | **dawn** | the Targum's word for shachar in Iyov, Mishlei and Tehillim (Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur); perhaps related to kritzah, winking, dawn being the small sign that daylight is coming (Rabbi Moshe Kosover of Beit Chilkiyah) | [morning-shachar-boker-tzafra.md](entries/morning-shachar-boker-tzafra.md) |
| קרית ארבע | Kiryas Arba | **City of Four, City of Arba** | the older name (Yehoshua 14:15); "four" for a list of fours (Bereishis Rabbah 58:4) or the personal name of the giants' father (Rashi to Yehoshua 14:15) | [hebron-chevron-kiryas-arba-mamre-eshkol.md](entries/hebron-chevron-kiryas-arba-mamre-eshkol.md) |
| קרן | keren | **horn** | a horn, and a corner as something that juts out from a smooth surface (Malbim, Rabbi Mecklenburg); where two sides collide, from the root of strong impact (Pappenheim); in Tanach the corners of the Altar | [corner-peah-keren-zavit-pinah.md](entries/corner-peah-keren-zavit-pinah.md) |
| קרן | keren | **horn** | the general horn, attached or detached, and a solid horn even detached (Ramban); by extension a ray, strength, a corner and principal; the meeting point of opposing forces, a fork in the road (Rabbi Moshe Shapiro) | [horn-shofar-keren-yovel-chatzotzros.md](entries/horn-shofar-keren-yovel-chatzotzros.md) |
| קרקע | karka | **floor** | not a word for land at all in Biblical Hebrew but the floor under a building or a sea, only later near-synonymous with eretz and adamah (Rabbi Avraham Bedersi) | [earth-taivel-arka-cheled.md](entries/earth-taivel-arka-cheled.md) |
| קשה | kashah | **hard** | the general word, covering both rigid and difficult; the hard work of Mitzrayim; kin to yesh, existence, and to gishah, impact, since only the solid is felt (Rav Hirsch); a family of hard things (Pappenheim) | [hard-kashah-kashiach-perech.md](entries/hard-kashah-kashiach-perech.md) |
| קשיח | kashiach | **cruel, callous** | cruelty rather than hardness of substance (Ibn Ezra, Radak), specifically estrangement from one a person should love (Rabbi Shlomo Ibn Melech); a portmanteau of kashah and sach, removing the harshness from one's thoughts (Metzudas Tzion) | [hard-kashah-kashiach-perech.md](entries/hard-kashah-kashiach-perech.md) |
| קשירה | keshirah | **tie, bind** | tying to which the thing tied consents, as conspirators willingly join one another in a kesher (Malbim); used concretely of tefillin and a string, figuratively of souls tied together | [tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md](entries/tying-keshirah-asirah-kafut.md) |

| תרדמה | tardeimah | **deep sleep** | sleep that overpowers a man and takes him unwilling (Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim), the senses tied down as though fettered (Rav Hirsch); the deepest of the three (Ibn Ezra, Radak); the Netziv disagrees and makes it the lighter sleep of one just dropping off | [sleep-sheinah-tardeimah-tenumah.md](entries/sleep-sheinah-tardeimah-tenumah.md) |

| תרועה | | see entry | one of the *divine judgment* words | [judgment-din-rachamim.md](entries/judgment-din-rachamim.md) |
| תרים | tarim | **scouts** | the men on that positive errand; Tanach never calls Moshe's men meraglim | [spying-latur-leragel.md](entries/spying-latur-leragel.md) |
| תרנגול | tarnegol | **rooster** | absent from Tanach, standard throughout the Mishnah; Rabbi Meir HaLevi Abulafia notes it contains the letters of Nergal, the rooster-shaped Kuthean idol, and Rabbi Ernest Klein derives it from Akkadian tar-lugallu | [rooster-gever-sechvi-tarnegol.md](entries/rooster-gever-sechvi-tarnegol.md) |
| תרע | tera | **gate** | the standard Targumic Aramaic for shaar, and also Targum's word for petach, "opening"; which Rabbi Eliyahu HaBachur suggests comes from the Aramaic sense of breaching, a gate seemingly being a break in the wall | [gate-shaar-tera-bava.md](entries/gate-shaar-tera-bava.md) |
| תרעלה | | see entry | one of the *poison* words | [poison-eres-rosh-chamat-sam-hamaves.md](entries/poison-eres-rosh-chamat-sam-hamaves.md) |
| תרפים | terafim | **things that rot** | named from rotting, since they can go putrid | [idols-elilim-gilulim-shikutzim.md](entries/idols-elilim-gilulim-shikutzim.md) |
| תשובה | teshuvah | **repentance** | repentance precisely because it is a return, to man's natural sin-free state whether or not he was ever there before (Rabbi Klein); it goes back to past deeds to make amends, as hashavah fills a hole | [return-shuv-chazarah.md](entries/return-shuv-chazarah.md) |
| תשועה | teshuah | **salvation** | salvation answering a cry (shav'ah) for help; kin to ש-פ-ע, it concerns property and economic freedom, so often military victory over outside conquerors (Rav Hirsch) | [salvation-yeshuah-teshuah-hatzalah-purkan.md](entries/salvation-yeshuah-teshuah-hatzalah-purkan.md) |
| תשוקה | | see entry | one of the *drinking* words | [drinking-shtiyah-hashkaah-gemiah.md](entries/drinking-shtiyah-hashkaah-gemiah.md) |
| תשורה | teshurah | **showpiece gift** | a hapax; the tribute people look at (shur) and sing (shir) over, the most honorable and eye-catching present (Midrash Shocher Tov, Wertheimer); a kind of minchah given on coming to a navi or holy man for a berachah or a prophecy (Malbim) | [gift-minchah-matanah-shai.md](entries/gift-minchah-matanah-shai.md) |
| תשי | | see entry | one of the *forgetting* words | [forgetting-shachach-nashah.md](entries/forgetting-shachach-nashah.md) |

---

## Part 2: the entries, with their full rulings


### action

**גישה / קירוב**: approach | gishah, gisha, vayigash, higish, higishah, nigash, kiruv, keiruv | [approach-gishah-kiruv.md](entries/approach-gishah-kiruv.md)

*Gishah* is **to approach** in the strong sense: coming right up to something, and usually across a gap of standing or in awe of it. *Kiruv* is **to draw near** or **bring closer**, a step taken while still on the way, between parties on a level. So when Yehudah *vayigash* to the viceroy (Bereishis 44:18), Rabbi Klein's own conclusion, drawn twice and marked each time as what "it seems," is that he came up close and personal rather than merely nearer, and that he did so very deliberately, as a further step in his campaign for Binyamin's release; on the first of those readings, Rabbi Klein says, Yehudah may even have come close in a threatening way, as certain midrashic sources imply. In Aramaic the distinction disappears: Targum typically renders both by *kiruv* cognates.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Default: גישה "approached," קרב "drew near" or "brought near." Where the two
  stand in one pasuk, as at Vayikra 2:8, the English must show two stages: "he
  brings it near to the kohen, and the kohen brings it up to the mizbeiach."
- Trap: English "approach" and "come close" will each cover both words. If a
  passage argues from the Torah's choice of one over the other (Devarim 25:1
  against Malachi 3:5; Vayikra 18:6), the rendering has to keep them apart or the
  argument evaporates.
- ויגש in Bereishis 44:18 is "then Yehudah came right up to him," not "approached
  him," if the derashos on his boldness are in play.
- קרבן stays "*korban*" or "offering," never "sacrifice of drawing near"; the
  etymology belongs in a note.
- Do not import the contrast into Aramaic. Targum renders both by *kiruv*
  cognates (Bereishis 18:23, 33:6, 44:18 for *gishah*; Bereishis 20:4, Shemos
  14:10, Vayikra 1:2 for *kiruv*), so a Targum-based argument cannot carry it.
- Modern *kiruv*, "outreach," is a borrowed use; keep it transliterated and do not
  read it back into a pasuk.

**חמוש / חלוץ / מזוין / זין / ויירק / חומש / חלצים / אזן**: armed | chamush, chamushim, chomesh, chimesh, chalutz, chalutzim, chalatzim, chalitzah | [armed-chamush-chalutz-mezuyan.md](entries/armed-chamush-chalutz-mezuyan.md)

All three mean **armed**, and the Midrashim equate them outright: *Bamidbar Rabbah* 13:20 says *chamushim* means *chalutzim*, while *Mechilta d'Rabbi Yishmael* to Shemos 13:18 and *Shemos Rabbah* 20:19 say it means *mezuyanim*. *Chamush* is the Chumash's word (Shemos 13:18), tied by the grammarians to the *chomesh*, the part of the body where a weapon is typically girded, and by the derashos to *chamesh*, five. *Chalutz* is, on Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim's reading, the **vanguard**, the men drawn out to go at the head of the army. *Mezuyan* is post-biblical, from Aramaic *zayin*, a weapon. Targum renders *chamush* in all four places by *zariz*, ready at a moment's notice, and often renders *chalutz* the same way; Onkelos gives *vayarek* of Avraham by *zariz* too. At Shemos 13:18 "armed" and "a fifth of them" are both live readings of one word.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Shemos 13:18: render "armed" with Ramban and the peshat, and footnote the
  Mechilta's "one in five." Do not try to carry both in the English; a hedge
  like "arrayed in fifties" satisfies neither reading.
- Trap: English "armed" absorbs all three, and "arms" absorbs *zayin*, *neshek*
  and *klei zayin*. Where the words stand together (the Midrashim equating
  *chamushim* with *chalutzim* and with *mezuyanim*), that flattening is the
  point and is fine; where a source distinguishes them (Malbim to Yehoshua
  4:12), give *chalutzim* "the vanguard" or "the men drawn out" and keep
  "armed" for *chamushim*.
- *Chalutzim* of Bamidbar 32 is "as a vanguard" or "in the lead, armed," not
  "pioneers"; whether the modern sense grows out of the biblical one is itself
  disputed (the *Aspaklaria* exchange above), so it does not belong in a
  translation of the pasuk.
- *Chomesh* in Shmuel is the "lower abdomen" or "the fifth rib," with Sanhedrin
  49a; do not render it "belly," which loses the anatomical precision the Gemara
  is supplying.
- Bereishis 41:34, *v'chimesh*: pick one, "he shall take a fifth" (Rashbam, Ibn
  Ezra, Radak) or "he shall organize" (Onkelos, Rashi), and name the other in
  a note. The two readings are not compatible in one English clause.
- *Zayin* stays transliterated where the source is playing on the letter-name
  (the *Avos d'Rabbi Nosson* passage, the absence of zayin from Tehillim 91);
  elsewhere it is "weapon."

**חרש / חשב / רקם / אמן / חרש**: artisan | charash, choresh, charashim, choshev, maaseh choshev, rokem, roikem, rikmah | [artisan-charash-choshev-rokem.md](entries/artisan-charash-choshev-rokem.md)

The Torah's three words for Betzalel's and Oholiav's skills (Shemos 35:35, 38:23) are not synonyms. *Charash* is the **craftsman** who reshapes raw material, wood, stone or metal. *Choshev* is the **designer**, who plans and combines finished materials into a figured work, hence *maaseh choshev* brocade. *Rokem* is the **embroiderer**, working in colors. Both are embroidery, and the Gemara (Yoma 72b) distinguishes them by how many faces the work shows.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Shemos 35:35 and 38:23: "craftsman, designer and embroiderer" is the safe set,
  but in a Mishkan passage keep *maaseh choshev* and *maaseh rokem*
  transliterated with a gloss. Rashi and the Rambam disagree about which is
  which, so an English word commits the translation to one side silently.
- Trap: "embroiderer" absorbs *choshev* and *rokem* together, and "craftsman"
  absorbs *charash* and *uman*. Where the Torah lists all three, three distinct
  English words are required.
- *Charash* in a navi's list of exiles (Melachim II 24:14): "craftsmen," not
  "smiths," since the word covers wood, stone and metal alike.
- *Chacham charashim* (Yeshayahu 3:3): render it and footnote the machlokes.
  "Skilled artisan" follows Ibn Ezra and the Gra; "master craftsman" follows
  Radak; "one wise in Torah" follows Rashi and the Gemara. Do not blend them.
- Aramaic *charash* as sorcerer must never be rendered "craftsman"; when both
  senses are in play in one sugya, transliterate.

**קידה / כריעה / השתחוויה / סגידה**: bowing | kidah, kida, kiddah, kriah, keriah, keri'ah, kriyah, hishtachavaah | [bowing-kidah-kriah-hishtachavaah.md](entries/bowing-kidah-kriah-hishtachavaah.md)

The Gemara (Megillah 22b, Berachos 34b) teaches that the three are three kinds of bowing: *kidah* is bowing the face, *kriah* is kneeling, and *hishtachavaah* is full prostration with hands and feet stretched out. Maharsha explains that each bows the head and some add more: *kidah* with the body otherwise erect, *kriah* on the knees, *hishtachavaah* stretched out on the floor. *Segidah* is Aramaic for *hishtachavaah* according to Radak; Malbim holds that the act may be the same but the purpose differs.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Trap: English "bow" absorbs all four. Where *kidah* and *hishtachavaah* stand
  together, as in *vayikod ha'ish vayishtachu* (Bereishis 24:26), "bowed and
  prostrated himself" keeps the Gemara's two distinct acts; "bowed and bowed
  down" loses them.
- "Worship" for *hishtachavaah* hides the physical act the Gemara defines and
  Malbim's point that it gives honor. In Yeshayahu 44:17, where *segidah* and
  *hishtachavaah* appear together, Malbim's reading needs two different words.

**בוא / בא / ביאה / הליכה / הלך / אתה**: coming | bo, boh, biah, bi'ah, lavo, lehavi, lech, leich | [coming-biah-halichah-atah.md](entries/coming-biah-halichah-atah.md)

*Bo* is **come**: it looks at the destination, and, as Rabbi Shlomo Pappenheim explains, it covers both the arriving and the being on the way. *Lech* is **go**. Just how the pair divides is not settled: the Tosafists' reading of the makkos pesukim seems to suggest that *bo* somehow implies entering where *lech* does not, and Rabbi Klein offers two theories of his own, that *bo* fixes on the destination and *lech* on the place of departure, or else that *halichah* names the act of walking while *biah* names a change of place however it came about. He adds that a concordance would have to be consulted to see how well any of these theories pans out. *Atah* is **arrive**: like *bo* it faces the destination, but it names only the arrival and never the journey (Rabbi Pappenheim, cited by Malbim). *Bo* and *atah* are not interchangeable.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Keep the English pair honest: *bo* is "come," *lech* is "go." Where the same
  parashah alternates them, as the makkos do, hold the pair even when English
  idiom would prefer otherwise, because the Tosafists' reading of *bo el
  Pharaoh* depends on it.
- *Bo el Pharaoh* in a work that follows the Tosafists or the Zohar is better
  rendered "come in to Pharaoh," which keeps the sense of entering.
- *Atah*: "arrive," "has come," "came upon." Not a plain "come," which throws
  away the finality.
- Trap: English "come" absorbs both *bo* and *atah*, and English "go" will
  quietly absorb *bo* whenever the sentence is about travel. If a phrase has
  both (a prophecy of what will *atah* to one who *ba*), render the *bo* as
  coming and the *atah* as arriving, and do not smooth the two together.
- Participles: *ba* of a man still on the road is "coming," not "has come." The
  Rachel and Yosef pesukim are the test cases.

**בקיעה / קריעה / גזירה / חתיכה / בתר / נתח / פתיתה / מילה / פלח / קטב / פרימה / גדע / קציצה / קטיפה / כרת**: cutting | bokea, bekiah, bakia, korea, kriah, kriyah, keriah, gozer | [cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md](entries/cutting-bokea-korea-gozer.md)

*Bokea* is **splitting open**, from the inside outward. *Korea* is **tearing**, and specifically of something soft, by a force from outside. *Gozer* is **cutting** with a blade through something thick, and by extension **decreeing**. *Chatichah* is the ordinary Rabbinic word for **cutting**, originally cutting in half. The splitting of the sea is called by all three verbs in different sources, each saying something different about who did what to what.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Keep the three sea-verbs distinct in English: "split open" for *bokea*, "tear"
  or "rend" for *korea*, "cut" for *gozer*. *Krias Yam Suf* is conventionally
  "the splitting of the sea," which is fine as a fixed English phrase, but where
  a passage is asking why the Oral Torah says *korea*, render it "tearing" so the
  question survives translation.
- Trap: "split" will swallow both *bokea* and *korea*, and English has no natural
  way to mark inside-out against outside-in. Where a source turns on that
  difference, say it: "burst open from within," "torn open from without."
- *Gezeirah* in a mussar or halachic passage is "decree." Where a source plays on
  the cutting sense (Tehillim 136:13 and Rav Hirsch there), let the English carry
  both: "cut" in the body, "decreed" noted alongside.
- *Kriah* for mourning stays transliterated or reads "rending," never "cutting."
- *Netach* and *chatichah* both reach English "piece." If a passage counts pieces,
  *besarim* is two, *nesachim* is many.
- Where *primah* and *kriah* appear together, mark the difference: one tear that
  unravels the whole against one tear that removes one piece.

**ריקוד / כרכור / פיזוז / פזז / רקד / מרקד / מכרכר / מפזז**: dancing | rikud, rikkud, rikod, rekidah, miraked, mirakedin, kirkur, micharker | [dancing-rikud-kirkur-pizuz.md](entries/dancing-rikud-kirkur-pizuz.md)

*Rikud* is the general word for **dancing**, and per Rabbi Moshe Tedeschi-Ashkenazi it names the joy that is the occasion for it; the other two, it seems to Rabbi Klein, describe specific acts of dancing. *Kirkur* (*micharker*) is the footwork: **whirling, capering**, which Rabbi Yosef Kara glosses as circular motion. *Pizuz* (*mifazez*) is the wild, fast part: **prancing** or **leaping about**, the hands and fingers moving with the feet. At Shmuel II 6:14 David is only *micharker*, and at 6:16, through Michal's eyes, he is *mifazez umecharker*. For Rabbi Zev Atlas, the added verb names what truly irked Michal.

**Rendering guidance.**

- Shmuel II 6:14 "David was whirling with all his might before Hashem"; 6:16
  "leaping and whirling before Hashem." The pair must be two English words, and
  the extra verb must appear only in the second pasuk.
- Trap: English "dance" absorbs all three. Keep "dance" for *rikud*, which is
  the neutral term, and force "whirl" or "caper" and "leap" or "prance" for the
  other two wherever they stand together (Rambam, *Hilchos Lulav* 8:13).
- Second trap: Rambam's 8:13 against 8:14 is a register distinction; if the
  sages "danced" while the crowd "pranced and whirled," the English carries what
  the Hebrew carried. Do not level the two halachos.
- *Rikud* in the halachos of Shabbos is a term of art. Where the Yerushalmi's
